subject.title: Feature Request: Gateway lifecycle hooks (onSubagentComplete, onToolCallThreshold, onTurnComplete)

question: Should subagent completion, turn completion, and tool-call-threshold behavior be exposed to workspace/internal HOOK.md hooks, kept in typed plugin hooks, or split between the two surfaces?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but payload shape, plugin authority, workspace-hook trust, event ordering, and threshold configuration are public API and security-boundary choices.

options.title: Split Observation From Control
options.body: Expose narrow observation-only internal hooks for subagent and turn completion while keeping mutation, prompt injection, and sensitive lifecycle control in typed plugin hooks.

options.title: Keep Plugin-Only
options.body: Declare typed plugin hooks the supported lifecycle surface and close or narrow the workspace-hook request accordingly.

options.title: Design Unified Lifecycle Model
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define a combined internal/plugin lifecycle event model including threshold configuration semantics.

recommendation.title: Split Observation From Control
recommendation.body: Expose narrow observation-only internal hooks for subagent and turn completion while keeping mutation, prompt injection, and sensitive lifecycle control in typed plugin hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice centers on hook contracts and lifecycle/security boundaries where current file history and related PRs point most strongly.
